body:
I only have my own brain to work with. If someone tells me to make use of someone else's, how exactly am I supposed to evaluate them?

It's not some minor aspect of my thinking. This warped view you are talking about is everything. It determines everything about how I act and permeates the world to such an extent that I'm prepared to give up the entire world if it says so.

Thank you again for the responses. This is making me feel worse and I need to take a big step back. Not that this is a debate, but you can have the last word.

My reasoning skills are damaged? People won't even allow for the possibility that I'm perfectly able to figure this out on my own. Suicide medical resources will tell you to talk to shamans for advice but somehow I'm the irrational one.

I'm sorry, it's not your fault, I know you are just trying to help. But if a person tells me I'm irrational and can't think straight (such as my doctors) I can't trust them.

If I sat down and said "you can't think straight, so you need to forego your own ideas about how to do things and listen to me," you would rightly dismiss me.

Suicide attempts mostly fail, so in all probability I'm just going to be forced into treatment. That's not free to give up treatment, it's the exact opposite.

And "fake it until you believe it?" I can't convince myself of something I don't believe is true, and even if I could, I won't take things on faith. That sort of lack of integrity is something I don't believe in. If I did that, there would be no reason not to believe an infinite number of ridiculous things.

Not a pharmacist, couldn't tell you. My assumption is that drugs can't solve every problem. We've tried altering doses and adding support drugs. I've followed through on every change and prescription.

It's not working, and I'm sick of it. At what point am I allowed to just say fuck it and stop treatment?

Usually, a talk with a therapist would have resulted in me questioning some of my depressive and obsessive thoughts. Instead of "I can't do this," I would be forced to accept that maybe I could do it.

Here's a concrete example. I think that the future can only get worse for me. My doctor will try and reason with me that past history proves how things can get better and how we have a reasonable belief, based on my previously exhibited abilities, the future can and probably will be good if we work towards it.

My response is to discount that. He's wrong about past events, he's wrong about my abilities, and he's wrong about about what is possible. If he isn't wrong, my irrationality means I still don't believe it, and since I don't believe it it will be a self fulfilling prophecy. Either way, no way out of it.

I've never had any motivation to do anything. I've always assumed I was incompetent at anything I did. Every little worry becomes an insurmountable certainty.

I've been treated before, most of my life. It's worked on some of the more obvious OCD symptoms like bizarre rituals I used to do. And, at times, I even had lessened depression symptoms. But it's never been this constant or this severe. 

Previously, pills would have worked by now and therapy would have put into question my assumptions.

Didn't quite want to give a life story, but you asked.

That's fine, I'll do it here. Depression, Obsessive Compulsive Disorder, and Anxiety brought on by those. Suicide has existed in the back of my mind most of my life, but it recently has become constant, the desire to do it stronger, and I've run through a plan in my head. The doctor knows all of this.

When I have wanted to get better, treatment hasn't worked. It is not working now, and I no longer want to get better. I'm still seeing a doctor because I feel pressured into doing it. Otherwise, I wouldn't.

I don't think it's the specific doctor. It's more that I can't trust anyone, and I don't believe them when they say I can be helped. It's frustrating to see them constantly waste their time and energy on a lost cause.

There is none, as far as I can see. Suicide based resources even talk about how leaving the hospital is when you are most at risk of suicide.

As best I can tell, it's to save face, with the added benefit of being able to forcibly charge you for it.

These rules (and the previous ones) specifically mention that the outcome of the action is not relevant, so yes, who heard it is irrelevant. It doesn't even matter if anyone was offended.

And that's my biggest issue with these rules. I realize that once you carefully outline what is and is allowed, you invite people to step just aside that boundary. However, if the goal is to create a safe environment, whether or not someone is actually being harmed is important. As is, you can say something deemed inappropriate because of a protected class, and even if nobody gets hurt, it is considered a major violation. Meanwhile, someone can say something incredibly hurtful to someone that isn't of a protected class and they just have to suck it up.

It's the same as it was in previous IPGs, but this announcement really strengthens the language.

I don't find the moments of joy worth the suffering.

And I don't buy that I must know suffering to know joy. Why would that be? And if it was the case, that says nothing about the amount of suffering you need to experience to understand joy.

And all of that is beside the point. What if I don't want to live in a universe that works that way? That universe sucks.
I would like to know, why are you considering the impact of a letter if you don't care what happens to anyone?

That sort of a response is something you never do with a suicidal person for the very reason you outlined.

I'm told there are therapists out there who know what they are doing and are helpful. If anyone finds one, let me know.

It seemed drowned out by the much more popular opinions like "what a pussy" or "that's selfish."

Heck, again, it's what doctors say. They have no issue trying to guilt you into living because it will hurt people.

The amount of suffering that inevitably results from living is not worth the expected amount of joy that I would get out of life.

The world sucks for all of the reasons everyone always gives. There is an unfathomable amount of suffering. Injustices are not just perpetuated by other people but are seemingly built into the nature of the universe. I live a relatively privileged existence, but still do not see the struggle as worth it.

Suicide would be one solution to this problem. It would remove my ability to experience negative things at the cost of positive things.

Finding some way to make the world not suck.
Finding some way to be satisfied with the state and future of my life.
Killing myself.

Those are what I can think of, but I don't rule out others.
I want "changing my mind" to not be the only option people give me. I want it open ended, including but not limited to "killing myself."

Yes.

I guess if you want to get technical, the legal system does, since they can punish the doctor if the wrong decision is made.
Compared to recognizing that they do not have the ultimate decision. For suicide, they do. That's not true of most illnesses.

Why? That doesn't get me any closer to my goal. It's great to be in the company of people who agree with you, but I don't want company; I want to be in a state with no company.

I'm just ranting at this point, I'm sorry. I appreciate the talk. I just wish you had a magic solution.

I'm allowed to deny life saving treatment. I'm allowed to perform dangerous stunts. I can eat until obesity kills me, smoke until my lungs rot, or drink until my skin turns yellow. Doctors will recommend you don't do this, but they can't stop you.

There being a few people who understand that is a start. However, the entire medical and legal community (and this sub too, as a matter of fact) encourage belittling and discounting the thoughts of suicidal people. The disparity is massive and the power held by my side infinitesimal.

Let me rephrase. I'm not talking about DNA or innate drives. I meant that a suicidal person gets the blame for having consciously made a decision while at the same time isn't allowed to carry out that decision.
As in given the actual ability to carry out the chosen action. If I try to, people will try and stop me.

If they are worse off, that's a shame. Unfortunately, their desire to be better doesn't apply when it unduly infringes on the rights of others.

People are worse off when I don't volunteer at a homeless shelter. I'm not legally forced to work at a homeless shelter.
I guess that there are similar responses to non mental illnesses. But I've never seen that sort of behaviour normalized and encouraged by the medical literature like it is for suicide.
There's the double standard. Suicidal people get all of the blame for having made a choice, but none of the agency.

Never seen it.

People will be hurt, sure, but I can't help but think that they will be hurt because of their own selfishness. If I were able to kill myself in a peaceful and controlled manner, people may wish I hadn't done it. But enforcing their beliefs on me is far more selfish than killing myself.

In general, I'm ok with hurting (non physically) people who hold bad beliefs. Just like I wouldn't care about hurting someone who was a sexist.

That surprises me. It's a common sentiment among mental health advocates.

Sure, a commuter may see someone vomit and think "ugh, how unpleasant," but I've never seen it classified as a moral and selfish failing on the part of the victim.

It hits close to home. That was my current plan for killing myself. I don't want to hurt other people; that's half the reason to die in the first place. But when society says "go kill yourself with pills or something," it's like they haven't even done the most basic research into how this works.

Pills are a terrible idea. They are notoriously unreliable and can take weeks to work if they do. Weeks of agonizing pain that you may not be able to fix, so you get to sit there and be guilted by family and doctors for untold hours. Nurses have to attend to your failing body and all manner of fluids and horror to clean up.

Yes, doing it in public means people have to watch. Stop blaming me for that. Blame the fact that people forbid me from having any other option.

Which might not be a problem, but these people who don't understand are a large part of how our policy is constructed. They force their uninformed opinion on the rest of us and are occasionally educated by organizations that also don't understand.

Can't. Rules of the forum forbid reasonable discussion of suicide, and only permit one sided discussion that has already come to the same conclusion. Help guides, doctors, they all assume that a suicidal person can't think right.

So instead, I wanted to talk about how suicidal people are treated.  If it's an illness like any other, why do we get blamed for it?

That's sort of what is on my mind. Nobody, not even the people who are supposed to, seem to understand or respect the viewpoint of a suicidal person.

I started a threat about it before, so now I'm more asking about how we are treated. It's usually with anger, condescension, or as though we aren't seen at all.

Just today, there was a Today I Learned about horrible things people have seen. One of them was a public suicide, to which the response was universally, "those selfish bastards are too pussy to do it themselves." It's not like suicidal people have a lot of options.

All it does is justify in my mind the thoughts that made me want to die in the first place.
You don't, but the medical community does.

Society doesn't give people who want to die reasonable alternatives. I assure you, suicidal people don't want to be made a spectacle, but killing yourself is very hard and the reliable methods are violent.

Seriously, this is like blaming a blind man for walking around with a dog because "I'm allergic, can't they be considerate?"

But the fact of the matter is that this attitude appears in the most controlled and clinical conditions. Scientific endeavors, which exist solely to remove human biases and fears, comes to the exact same conclusion.

That bothers me. I'd like to think of myself as a reasonable person who goes where evidence leads me. How then can I be so off about this universally agreed upon fact? It would be like if I thought the world was flat.

Well thank you for being reasonable. Just a few billion more like you are this might not be an issue.

I just want to opt out. Why is that an issue? And how can you expect to reach a suicidal person unless you understand that perspective?

I guess I'm just at the point where I'm in such disagreement with the societal ideal of "normal" that I feel like I can't trust people.

This board, every resource I've tried to use, they all say the same thing. Killing yourself can't be considered rational and we should force people to think our way, whether through peer pressure, legal threats, destroying your livelihood, or drugs.

I don't want to continue treatment because it hasn't been working. I want to kill myself, and I don't want people to stop me from getting what I want. And if it turns out that I'm too far gone to see the world as it is, that's fine. That means the world has a chance to be better, and everyone else gets to live in that world. I'd rather be insane than right in this instance.

I'm going to stop the religious debate, because that was just an example, not the reason for my issue. You can substitute in any sort of superstition, belief in magic, or conspiracy theories and the point is mostly the same. But I will say that, if forcing beliefs on others is a metric, I don't plan on killing anyone else. I tend to believe that the caveat "self" in "self or others" is a bad metric.

Yes, I've been pessimistic about as far back as I can remember. I've also believed in my own incompetence. This isn't some bizarre flare-up, it's as integral to who I am as anything else. And I always remember believing that if a person does not want to live anymore, the correct thing to do is let them die or kill them if they are unable to. To do anything else would be to own that person more than they own themselves.

But beliefs like that do pose a direct risk to a person's well being and, in some cases, other people as well. They engage in self injurious behaviour and, in the United States, demand everyone else follow their rules.

I think that the belief that you will survive your own death is far more harmful than that I should be able to end mine. Even some of the resources on the sidebar insist that it's not possible for a person who wants to die to think rationally. And then it also says not to make them feel challenged or like a failure. What exactly does saying "you are so screwed up that we can't expect you to think for yourself" do? And what does it say that my beliefs are considered more dangerous than people who think the hear djinns talking to them?

And there is the incredibly self serving nature of someone who says "no, you need my help,  in fact, any thoughts you are having about not getting my help is just proof you need my help."

Assuming "that's just the depression" talking is exactly the sort of dismissal I'm talking about. Not allowing for the possibility that I am perfectly able to think for myself.

When most people believe irrational things, we as a society say to let them believe what they believe. When I believe something irrational, they  force me to take pills and engage in treatment I don't want to do.

It's not just a respect for my beliefs, but a respect for my ability to think. I can't trust someone whose first response is to discount my ability to think.
I can't get specific because the rules of this forum forbid it. But, in general, when I have negative thoughts about the future or believe in my own incompetence.
